name: add_note
doc:

add a note to the exception

name: with_traceback
doc:
Exception.with_traceback(tb) --
set self.__traceback__ to tb and return self.

name: abs

doc: Return an AsyncIterator for an AsyncIterable object.

name: all
doc:
Return True if bool(x) is True for all values x in the iterable.

If the iterable is empty, return True.

name: anext
doc:

Return the next item from the async iterator.  If default is given and the async
iterator is exhausted, it is returned instead of raising StopAsyncIteration.

name: any
doc:
Return True if bool(x) is True for any x in the iterable.

If the iterable is empty, return False.

name: bin
doc:
Return the binary representation of an integer.

>>> bin(2796202)
'0b1010101010101010101010'

name: as_integer_ratio
doc:
Return a pair of integers, whose ratio is equal to the original int.

The ratio is in lowest terms and has a positive denominator.

name: bit_count
doc:
Number of ones in the binary representation of the absolute value of self.

Also known as the population count.

name: bit_length
doc:
Number of bits necessary to represent self in binary.

>>> bin(37)
'0b100101'

name: conjugate
doc: Returns self, the complex conjugate of any int.

Call sys.breakpointhook(*args, **kws).  sys.breakpointhook() must accept
whatever arguments are passed.

Append a single item to the end of the bytearray.

item
  The item to be appended.

doc:
B.capitalize() -> copy of B

Return a copy of B with only its first character capitalized (ASCII)
and the rest lower-cased.

doc:
Return a centered string of length width.

Padding is done using the specified fill character.

doc: Remove all items from the bytearray.

doc: Return a copy of B.

Return the number of non-overlapping occurrences of subsection sub in

Decode the bytearray using the codec registered for encoding.

encoding
  The encoding with which to decode the bytearray.

Return True if B ends with the specified suffix, False otherwise.
With optional start, test B beginning at that position.

name: expandtabs
doc:
Return a copy where all tab characters are expanded using spaces.

If tabsize is not given, a tab size of 8 characters is assumed.

name: extend
doc:
Append all the items from the iterator or sequence to the end of the bytearray.

iterable_of_ints
  The iterable of items to append.

Return the lowest index in B where subsection sub is found,

doc:
Create a bytearray object from a string of hexadecimal numbers.

Spaces between two numbers are accepted.
Example: bytearray.fromhex('B9 01EF') -> bytearray(b'\\xb9\\x01\\xef')

name: hex
doc:
Create a string of hexadecimal numbers from a bytearray object.

  sep
    An optional single character or byte to separate hex bytes.

doc:

Return the lowest index in B where subsection sub is found,
such that sub is contained within B[start,end].  Optional

doc:
Insert a single item into the bytearray before the given index.

index
  The index where the value is to be inserted.

name: isalnum
doc:
B.isalnum() -> bool

Return True if all characters in B are alphanumeric
and there is at least one character in B, False otherwise.

name: isalpha
doc:
B.isalpha() -> bool

Return True if all characters in B are alphabetic
and there is at least one character in B, False otherwise.

name: isascii
doc:
B.isascii() -> bool

Return True if B is empty or all characters in B are ASCII,
False otherwise.

name: isdigit
doc:
B.isdigit() -> bool

Return True if all characters in B are digits
and there is at least one character in B, False otherwise.

name: islower
doc:
B.islower() -> bool

Return True if all cased characters in B are lowercase and there is
at least one cased character in B, False otherwise.

name: isspace
doc:
B.isspace() -> bool

Return True if all characters in B are whitespace
and there is at least one character in B, False otherwise.

doc:
B.istitle() -> bool

Return True if B is a titlecased string and there is at least one
character in B, i.e. uppercase characters may only follow uncased

name: isupper
doc:
B.isupper() -> bool

Return True if all cased characters in B are uppercase and there is
at least one cased character in B, False otherwise.

doc:
Concatenate any number of bytes/bytearray objects.

Padding is done using the specified fill character.

name: lower
doc:
B.lower() -> copy of B

Return a copy of B with all ASCII characters converted to lowercase.

name: lstrip
doc:
Strip leading bytes contained in the argument.

If the argument is omitted or None, strip leading ASCII whitespace.

doc:
Return a translation table useable for the bytes or bytearray translate method.

The returned table will be one where each byte in frm is mapped to the byte at
the same position in to.

found, returns a 3-tuple containing the part before the separator, the

doc:
Remove and return a single item from B.

  index
    The index from where to remove the item.

doc:
Remove the first occurrence of a value in the bytearray.

value
  The value to remove.

name: removeprefix
doc:
Return a bytearray with the given prefix string removed if present.

If the bytearray starts with the prefix string, return
bytearray[len(prefix):].  Otherwise, return a copy of the original

Return a bytearray with the given suffix string removed if present.

empty, return bytearray[:-len(suffix)].  Otherwise, return a copy of

name: replace
doc:
Return a copy with all occurrences of substring old replaced by new.

  count
    Maximum number of occurrences to replace.

name: reverse
doc: Reverse the order of the values in B in place.

Return the highest index in B where subsection sub is found,

Return the highest index in B where subsection sub is found,

doc:
Return a right-justified string of length width.

Padding is done using the specified fill character.

doc:
Partition the bytearray into three parts using the given separator.

If the separator is found, returns a 3-tuple containing the part before the

doc:
Return a list of the sections in the bytearray, using sep as the delimiter.

  sep
    The delimiter according which to split the bytearray.

doc:
Strip trailing bytes contained in the argument.

If the argument is omitted or None, strip trailing ASCII whitespace.

name: splitlines
doc:
Return a list of the lines in the bytearray, breaking at line boundaries.

Line breaks are not included in the resulting list unless keepends is given and
true.

doc:
B.startswith(prefix[, start[, end]]) -> bool

Return True if B starts with the specified prefix, False otherwise.
With optional start, test B beginning at that position.

Strip leading and trailing bytes contained in the argument.

If the argument is omitted or None, strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace.

name: swapcase
doc:
B.swapcase() -> copy of B

Return a copy of B with uppercase ASCII characters converted
to lowercase ASCII and vice versa.

name: title
doc:
B.title() -> copy of B

Return a titlecased version of B, i.e. ASCII words start with uppercase
characters, all remaining cased characters have lowercase.

name: translate
doc:
Return a copy with each character mapped by the given translation table.

  table
    Translation table, which must be a bytes object of length 256.

name: upper
doc:
B.upper() -> copy of B

Return a copy of B with all ASCII characters converted to uppercase.

name: zfill
doc:
Pad a numeric string with zeros on the left, to fill a field of the given width.

The original string is never truncated.

doc:
Return whether the object is callable (i.e., some kind of function).

Note that classes are callable, as are instances of classes with a
__call__() method.

name: chr
doc: Return a Unicode string of one character with ordinal i; 0 <= i <= 0x10ffff.

doc:
Compile source into a code object that can be executed by exec() or eval().

The source code may represent a Python module, statement or expression.
The filename will be used for run-time error messages.

name: delattr
doc:
Deletes the named attribute from the given object.

delattr(x, 'y') is equivalent to ``del x.y``

doc: Create a new dictionary with keys from iterable and values set to value.

doc: Return the value for key if key is in the dictionary, else default.

doc: D.items() -> a set-like object providing a view on D's items

name: keys
doc: D.keys() -> a set-like object providing a view on D's keys

name: popitem
doc:
Remove and return a (key, value) pair as a 2-tuple.

Pairs are returned in LIFO (last-in, first-out) order.
Raises KeyError if the dict is empty.

name: setdefault
doc:
Insert key with a value of default if key is not in the dictionary.

Return the value for key if key is in the dictionary, else default.

name: update
doc:
D.update([E, ]**F) -> None.  Update D from mapping/iterable E and F.
If E is present and has a .keys() method, then does:  for k in E.keys(): D[k] = E[k]
If E is present and lacks a .keys() method, then does:  for k, v in E: D[k] = v
In either case, this is followed by: for k in F:  D[k] = F[k]

name: values
doc: D.values() -> an object providing a view on D's values

doc: Return the tuple (x//y, x%y).  Invariant: div*y + mod == x.

name: eval
doc:
Evaluate the given source in the context of globals and locals.

The source may be a string representing a Python expression
or a code object as returned by compile().

name: exec
doc:
Execute the given source in the context of globals and locals.

The source may be a string representing one or more Python statements
or a code object as returned by compile().

name: format
doc:
Return type(value).__format__(value, format_spec)

Many built-in types implement format_spec according to the
Format Specification Mini-language. See help('FORMATTING').

name: difference
doc:
Return the difference of two or more sets as a new set.

(i.e. all elements that are in this set but not the others.)

name: intersection
doc:
Return the intersection of two sets as a new set.

(i.e. all elements that are in both sets.)

name: isdisjoint
doc: Return True if two sets have a null intersection.

name: issubset
doc: Test whether every element in the set is in other.

name: issuperset
doc: Test whether every element in other is in the set.

name: symmetric_difference
doc:
Return the symmetric difference of two sets as a new set.

(i.e. all elements that are in exactly one of the sets.)

name: union
doc:
Return the union of sets as a new set.

(i.e. all elements that are in either set.)

Return the dictionary containing the current scope's global variables.

NOTE: Updates to this dictionary *will* affect name lookups in the current
global scope and vice-versa.

doc:
Return whether the object has an attribute with the given name.

This is done by calling getattr(obj, name) and catching AttributeError.

name: hash
doc:
Return the hash value for the given object.

Two objects that compare equal must also have the same hash value, but the
reverse is not necessarily true.

name: id
doc:
Return the identity of an object.

This is guaranteed to be unique among simultaneously existing objects.
(CPython uses the object's memory address.)

name: input
doc:
Read a string from standard input.  The trailing newline is stripped.

The prompt string, if given, is printed to standard output without a
trailing newline before reading input.

name: isinstance
doc:
Return whether an object is an instance of a class or of a subclass thereof.

check against. This is equivalent to ``isinstance(x, A) or isinstance(x, B)

doc:
Return whether 'cls' is derived from another class or is the same class.

A tuple, as in ``issubclass(x, (A, B, ...))``, may be given as the target to
check against. This is equivalent to ``issubclass(x, A) or issubclass(x, B)

doc:
Sort the list in ascending order and return None.

The sort is in-place (i.e. the list itself is modified) and stable (i.e. the
order of two equal elements is maintained).

original array is converted to C or Fortran order. For contiguous views,

doc: Return a readonly version of the memoryview.

doc:

Return the next item from the iterator. If default is given and the iterator

name: oct
doc:
Return the octal representation of an integer.

>>> oct(342391)
'0o1234567'

doc:

file is either a text or byte string giving the name (and the path

doc:
Equivalent to base**exp with 2 arguments or base**exp % mod with 3 arguments

Some types, such as ints, are able to use a more efficient algorithm when
invoked using the three argument form.

doc:
Prints the values to a stream, or to sys.stdout by default.

sep
  string inserted between values, default a space.

doc:
Return the canonical string representation of the object.

For many object types, including most builtins, eval(repr(obj)) == obj.

Round a number to a given precision in decimal digits.

The return value is an integer if ndigits is omitted or None.  Otherwise

name: add
doc:
Add an element to a set.

This has no effect if the element is already present.

name: difference_update
doc: Remove all elements of another set from this set.

name: discard
doc:
Remove an element from a set if it is a member.

Unlike set.remove(), the discard() method does not raise
an exception when an element is missing from the set.

name: intersection_update
doc: Update a set with the intersection of itself and another.

name: symmetric_difference_update
doc: Update a set with the symmetric difference of itself and another.

doc:
Sets the named attribute on the given object to the specified value.

setattr(x, 'y', v) is equivalent to ``x.y = v``

Assuming a sequence of length len, calculate the start and stop

doc:
Return a new list containing all items from the iterable in ascending order.

A custom key function can be supplied to customize the sort order, and the
reverse flag can be set to request the result in descending order.

doc: Return a version of the string suitable for caseless comparisons.

doc:

  The encoding in which to encode the string.

doc:
S.format_map(mapping) -> str

Return a formatted version of S, using substitutions from mapping.
The substitutions are identified by braces ('{' and '}').

doc:
Return True if the string is a decimal string, False otherwise.

A string is a decimal string if all characters in the string are decimal and
there is at least one character in the string.

name: isidentifier
doc:
Return True if the string is a valid Python identifier, False otherwise.

Call keyword.iskeyword(s) to test whether string s is a reserved identifier,
such as "def" or "class".

name: isnumeric
doc:
Return True if the string is a numeric string, False otherwise.

A string is numeric if all characters in the string are numeric and there is at
least one character in the string.

name: isprintable
doc:
Return True if all characters in the string are printable, False otherwise.

A character is printable if repr() may use it in its output.

name: sum
doc:
Return the sum of a 'start' value (default: 0) plus an iterable of numbers

When the iterable is empty, return the start value.
This function is intended specifically for use with numeric values and may

doc: Return a type's method resolution order.

name: vars
doc:
vars([object]) -> dictionary

Without arguments, equivalent to locals().
With an argument, equivalent to object.__dict__.
